ncr.part: PH-60 pump housing, ductile iron casting
ncr.initial_description: Linear crack about 35 mm long on the outer wall near the inlet flange, visible after rough machining. Dye penetrant shows a continuous line indication. 4 of 120 castings from lot GF-4410.
ncr.containment: Lot GF-4410 held. The 38 machined housings in WIP were dye-penetrant inspected: only the 4 already found show indications.

lab_report.sections: Two castings sectioned across the indication.
lab_report.findings: The indication follows the junction of two metal streams, with an oxide film and rounded edges along the interface. No branching and no intergranular path. The discontinuity does not extend through the wall; it reaches roughly 40% of the wall thickness.
lab_report.conclusion: Cold shut from low metal temperature or an interrupted pour at the meeting point of two flow fronts. Not a hot tear and not a service crack.

state.supplier_input: The pour log for GF-4410 shows two ladles with a 90-second delay between them on the shift with the defects; pouring-temperature records for the second ladle are missing. The supplier says the pyrometer was being recalibrated that shift.

supplier_initial_8d.D4_preliminary: Suspect interrupted pour during a ladle change; confirmation pending the missing temperature record reconstruction from the furnace log.
supplier_initial_8d.D5_planned: Add a maximum ladle-change interval to the pouring instruction and an automatic temperature log on the second ladle.

state.drawing: Inlet flange wall is pressure-retaining; hydrotest at 1.5 times rated pressure is done at the supplier. Casting quality class per drawing note 3.
state.customer_pressure_spec: Our customer's specification PS-60 requires every assembled pump to pass a 1.5 times rated pressure test at our plant and states that weld-repaired pressure-retaining castings are acceptable only with the customer's written approval and a radiograph record per casting.

casting_spec_CS_9.§6.2: Weld repair on pressure-retaining walls requires written customer approval and radiography after repair.
casting_spec_CS_9.§6.3: Cracks (hot tears, shrinkage cracks) may not be weld repaired on any wall.

state.hydrotest_record: Supplier hydrotest certificate for GF-4410: all castings passed.
state.engineer_comment: If it is a crack we scrap everything and stop the line; if it is a cold shut, maybe weld repair per the casting spec.

state: ENGINEERING MEMO EM-26-044: Request for deviation, zinc-flake coating on fastener FB-880. Coating spec CS-12 calls for a coating thickness of 8 to 12 µm. Supplier Tessellate Fasteners coated lot ZF-1102 (18,000 pcs) at 6 to 7 µm because of a line-speed setting error, reported by the supplier on 09/10. state: LINE TF-3 (thermoformed PP drink cups, food-contact) SHIFT LOG, 2026-09-18, SHIFT A. Customer: Initech Foods. Customer spec: zero tolerance for foreign material; process defects are managed under the supplier's own SOP.

SOP-FM-02 Foreign material: §2 Any visible foreign material in food-contact product: stop the line, hold product back to the last clean check, and notify QA. §3 Specks confirmed by QA as degraded polymer from the process (carbonised resin) are process defects, not foreign material; the line may continue with 100% vision inspection while the source is cleaned. §4 Material from an external source (metal, wood, insects, paper, other plastics) is always foreign material. §5 Only QA may classify a speck under §3; until then §2 applies.
06:00 Clean check: visual audit of 50 cups plus metal detector test pieces: PASS (QA tech S. Grant).
06:10 Extruder restarted after a 40-minute film break (Op D. Russo).
06:40 [Op D. Russo] Black specks in cup walls, maybe 1 in 50 cups, started after the extruder restart.
06:55 [Op M. Lee] Those look like burnt resin to me; the screen changer was running hot after the restart. Kept running, pulling cups by hand.
07:20 [Op D. Russo] Found one speck that looks shiny, could be a metal flake. Put it in a bag for QA.

07:45 [QA tech S. Grant] Examined 12 specks under the microscope: 11 are carbonised polymer. The shiny one is sent to the lab; not yet identified. Line stopped at 07:50 pending the lab result. Product since the 06:00 clean check on hold.
08:30 Metal detector test pieces: PASS (QA tech S. Grant).
09:30 [Lab, R. Omar] Shiny particle: carbonised polymer with a glossy surface film. No metal detected by SEM-EDS.
09:40 [QA tech S. Grant] Classified as a process defect per §3. Line restarted with 100% vision inspection; screen changer cleaned.
10:15 [Maintenance, P. Aydin] Screen changer heater band controller replaced; melt temperature now stable.
11:00 [QA tech S. Grant] Held cups from 06:00 to 07:50 released after 100% vision sort; 214 cups with specks scrapped.
11:30 [Vision system report] Since 09:40 the vision system has rejected 38 cups for specks; reject rate falling each hour; no rejects since 10:50.
12:00 [Customer service] Initech Foods informed by email of the morning event, the lab result and the sort; customer asked for the vision-system data and a short 8D by Friday.
12:15 [Production planner] Order 44-2210 for Initech Foods remains on schedule; no shortage expected.

complaint.text: Plating is peeling off the knob skirt after our 48 h humidity test on 6 of 30 pieces from lot K-7730. Blisters first, then flaking. Please investigate and send an 8D.

Packaging: returnable dunnage reused without inspection.

Moulding: silicone mould-release spray used on tool T-31, contrary to the plating-grade process sheet that forbids release agents.

state.etch_bath_log: Line P1: titrations missing weeks 35 and 36; line P2: complete.
state.process_note: Plating adhesion on ABS depends on etch quality and on a clean moulded surface; silicone mould release is a well-known cause of poor adhesion. Both factors produce the same blister-then-flake appearance.

state.plating_line_P1_notes: P1 etch bath was replenished on estimate in weeks 35 and 36 while the titration kit was being replaced; the chemist's week-37 titration found the bath back within range after a correction.
state.other_lots: Lot K-7728 (moulded on T-31 in week 35, plated on P2 in week 36) and lot K-7733 (T-31, week 37, plated on P1 in week 37) have had no complaints; both are still at the customer's warehouse.
state.tape_test_sop: FI-12: one tape adhesion test per plating lot on five knobs; changed informally to one test per week in August.
state.customer_history: KN-5 had no adhesion complaints in the previous twelve months.

state: Analyst narrative, case INV-2026-0218. Personal account of A. Moreno (student, 22). In three weeks the account received many incoming transfers from unrelated individuals in different cities, several with references such as 'deposit for phone' and 'concert tickets'. Each incoming transfer was forwarded within hours, partly to a crypto exchange account in the customer's name and partly to two accounts abroad. Two of the senders have since filed fraud complaints with their banks saying they never received the goods they paid for. When called, the customer said: 'I help people buy things online, I just pass it on and keep a small commission.' He added that he found the 'payment processing assistant' role through a social media job advert and has never met his employer. Account opened eight months ago with student loan credits only.

typology.instructions: Which typology best fits the account activity described?

criteria.money_mule: Account used to receive and forward funds for others, often recruited

explanation_plausibility.instructions: How plausible is the customer's explanation as an account of legitimate activity?

criteria.definition: Contradicted by the evidence
Possible in theory, nothing supports it
Some supporting facts
Consistent with the evidence

recruitment_described.instructions: Does the narrative say the customer was recruited through a job advert?

customer_possibly_deceived.instructions: Does the narrative suggest the customer may himself have been deceived or exploited?

typology.note: Receive-and-forward within hours, a commission, recruitment through an online job advert and an employer never met are classic mule indicators; the victims' complaints show fraud proceeds passing through.

explanation_plausibility.note: Senders reported non-delivery fraud, which contradicts 'helping people buy things' as legitimate activity → implausible; some rate it weak rather than contradicted.

recruitment_described.note: 'found the ... role through a social media job advert'.

customer_possibly_deceived.note: A student recruited by an unseen 'employer' through an advert fits a deceived mule, but he knowingly forwards funds for a commission, so experts differ on whether the narrative suggests exploitation or complicity.
